summary.countingMethod: Grouped review units:9 complete lesson claim sets,27 complete question/option/worked-answer sets,21 standalone formula cards,each glossary entry,and9 lesson analogy decisions. This is not a count of distinct atomic factual sentences.

corrections: Moving-average group-delay wording could imply every sinusoid is merely delayed: replaced it with phase-slope meaning and explicit amplitude/shape and sign-jump qualifications.
Frequency-response card admitted zero gain while assigning an undefined phase: constrained its phase-bearing expression to positive amplitude/gain and kept zero output as an explicit separate case.
Stability formula cards did not explicitly locate the initial previous-output value: defined the sample-index start and zero previous output within each standalone card.
Filter-tail glossary suggested IIR tails always decay: stated that unstable IIR tails need not decay.
Removed duplicate dsp-zero-extension from filters so the earlier independently reviewed signals entry owns the concept.
Removed duplicate finite-summation concept/aliases so the earlier signals finite-sum entry owns the concept.
Fixed wrong dictionary meanings for output mode,block size,weighted average,wrapped value and call overhead;added four precise terms and reworded ordinary page-size/tail-position/sum-rule phrases.
Added tap/taps aliases so the introduced FIR coefficient term remains directly accessible in later explanations.
gaps: The FIR design is a modest four-frequency demonstration, explicitly not a certified full-band specification. No complete automated band-extremum design workflow is taught.
General high-order pole/zero design,fixed-point implementation and device real-time guarantees remain outside the agreed scope.

formulaLintExceptions.reason: Inline mode="full" is actual API keyword code, permitted Rule6.
10Hz andminus6dB are plain numerical statements with units;scale=True is actual API keyword code,permitted Rule6.

glossaryCoverageExceptions: How it maps and Where it stops are required analogy headings,not technical terms.

df-lti-systems.rationale: The recipe compares weighted combinations and repeating a fixed rule later; the visible text supplies both exact tests and the callout explicitly excludes literal cooking linearity.

df-impulse-response.rationale: A clap illustrates temporal spreading; the callout explicitly distinguishes an actual discrete impulse and does not claim one measurement proves LTI.

df-convolution.rationale: The main text already traces each shifted scaled finite response with all numerical contributions; an additional comparison would repeat that direct mechanism.

df-moving-average.rationale: The three-day dashboard maps equal sliding weights and event spreading, while the limitation explicitly preserves fixed divisor and zero history.

df-frequency-response.rationale: Direct DC,quarter-rate and Nyquist examples plus the response equation teach gain/phase without a separate comparison; required qualifications remain visible.

df-fir-design.rationale: This is a concrete design/API/measurement procedure with explicit response checks and delay conditions; a comparison would not clarify the parameter conventions.

df-iir-feedback.rationale: Repeated partial estimate updates accurately map current input and previous output with decreasing influence; fixed weights and exact state are distinguished from human judgement.

df-stability-precision.rationale: The lesson is an invariant-bound argument and a concrete numeric-overflow counterexample; an analogy could blur mathematical boundedness and representable range.

df-block-processing.rationale: Reading across pages maps preserved context across delivery boundaries; finite exact filter state is explicit and page-length wording avoids an unrelated memory-page dictionary target.
